T.topic_fa: کوچک‌کردن بی‌صدا: مشتری از گرانی نمی‌رنجد، از فریب می‌رنجد
T.topic_en: The quiet shrink: customers forgive a higher price, not a hidden one
T.central_tension_fa: همه فکر می‌کنیم کوچک‌کردن بسته بی‌خطرتر از گران‌کردن است، چون کسی متوجه نمی‌شود؛ و داده‌ی فروش هم همین را نشان می‌دهد. ولی همان لحظه که مشتری بفهمد، دیگر قضیه پول نیست، فریب است. همان صرفه‌جویی، اعتماد را می‌خورد.
T.central_tension_en: We assume shrinking the pack is safer than raising the price, because no one notices, and sales data mostly agrees. But the moment customers do notice, it stops being about money and becomes about being fooled. Saying it out loud makes the problem almost disappear.
T.working_hook_fa: شکلات کوچک‌تر شد. جعبه همان ماند. کسی نفهمید. تا روزی که فهمید.
T.working_hook_en: Same box. Less chocolate. Nobody noticed. Until somebody did.

key_sources.claim: Downsizing judged unfair more often than an equivalent price rise (chocolate 44.4% vs 30.7%); without disclosure 69.3% vs 53% unfair, with clear disclosure the gap disappears (36.9% vs 35.4%). Driver: feeling deceived.
Summary of the same research: >7,000 participants; transparency and genuine cost reasons make changes acceptable; 'Being honest with customers is always the best policy.'
Decade of US scanner data: about 1.92% of products downsized, usually without a price cut; shoppers react more to price than to size, so downsizing works as a margin tool.
UK Toblerone 400g->360g and 170g->150g by widening gaps between peaks, packaging unchanged; Mondelez cited ingredient costs; public mockery.
Mondelez: '150g Toblerone is no longer being manufactured', it was 'only ever a short term response to cost increases'.
Austrian law in force 1 April 2026: retailers must show a 'less content, higher price' notice for 60 days when unit price rises >=3% with unchanged packaging.

T.framing_note: The idea is evergreen; research is the spark, not the story. Do not call the Evangelidis study 'new' (2023/24). Do not say 'nobody notices' as fact: say sales data barely moves (C02) and that most people, once told, feel cheated. One number on screen at most: the disclosure result (gap nearly vanishes when told) or 'the same price rise, judged fairer than the smaller pack'. Toblerone: state the facts (gaps widened, box unchanged, 2016) and that the maker later stopped the 150g bar, citing costs; do not claim the backlash caused it. Optional line: some countries now force a label 'less content, higher price' (do not need to name Austria; never name any Gulf location). Close with the practical rule: if you must cut, cut out loud: say what changed and why, or raise the price honestly; never hide it in the same box. No brand logos as AI objects; real Toblerone imagery only from owner upload, framed and credited.
